title: TraceQA driver protocol
description: Messages between the engine and a browser driver. JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line, over the driver's stdin and stdout. The engine is always the caller. A driver holds no logic: it does what it is told and reports what happened.

protocolVersion.description: The version the driver speaks. The engine refuses to continue when it differs from its own.

browsers.description: Browser names this driver can open.

exclusiveBrowsers.description: Browsers of which only one session can exist on the machine at a time, whichever process opens it. The engine never runs two of these at once.

Capabilities.description: What this browser session can do. The engine adapts to these instead of knowing browser names.

clipScreenshot.description: Can screenshot one rectangle of the page.

fullPageScreenshot.description: Can screenshot the whole scrollable page.

evalAllFrames.description: Can run a script in every frame, not only the top one.

crossOriginFrames.description: Can run a script inside frames from another origin.

parallelSessions.description: Can hold more than one session at a time.

setViewport.description: Can set an exact viewport size.

failedRequests.description: Reports requests for scripts, styles, data and frames that failed while the page loaded, in page.eval's requestsFailed. Absent means false.

evalAsync.description: page.eval accepts awaitPromise. Absent means false.

actionKinds.description: The action kinds page.act accepts. Absent or empty means page.act is not supported by this session.

eventKinds.description: What page.act reports about an action. Known values: navigation, popups, dialogs, downloads, console, network, dom. A kind that is not listed is not observed: an empty list for it in a page.act result does not mean nothing happened. Absent means none.

locale.description: BCP 47 language tag, for example en-US.

storageState.description: Cookies and stored values to put in place before the first page is loaded.

policy.description: The safety policy of a session that will be given page.act. A driver refuses page.act on a session opened without one, and a driver that cannot enforce a policy refuses to open a session that asks for one.

ActPolicy.description: What the browser of a session may do while it is being acted on. Enforced by the driver on the browser's own requests, so it does not depend on what a button is called. Unless `allowWrites` is true: every request whose method is not GET or HEAD is aborted, and every WebSocket is never connected and is closed. Whatever `allowWrites` says: a navigation of the top-level page to an origin that is not in `allowOrigins` is aborted, and a page that ends up at such an origin anyway (a redirect, which the browser follows without asking the driver) is taken back to the page it came from. A blocked request is reported in `failedRequests` with the failure `blocked_by_policy`. Pages are not given `navigator.serviceWorker`, because a service worker makes requests of its own that the driver cannot see; a worker that a page starts itself is not covered.

allowOrigins.description: Origins (scheme, host and port, for example http://127.0.0.1:4173) the top-level page may navigate to. At least one.

allowWrites.description: Let requests other than GET and HEAD through. Absent means false.

SessionStorageParams.description: Asks for the session's cookies and stored values, to save them after someone has signed in.

viewport.description: The viewport the session really has, when the driver could not give the one asked for. Absent means the one asked for.

policy.description: The policy the session enforces, as the driver understood it. Sent when the request carried one. A caller compares it with what it asked for and closes the session when they differ: a driver that does not know about policies would send none.

WaitUntil.description: load: the load event fired. settled: load fired and the network and DOM have been quiet for a short time.

status.description: HTTP status of the main document, when known.

loadComplete.description: False when the page's content arrived but its load event did not fire in time, for example because one image never arrived. The page is then read as it stands. Absent means true.

closedShadowRoots.description: How many closed shadow roots the page has once loaded. No script can read inside one, so the collector cannot list what they hold. Absent when the driver cannot tell, as only Chromium-based browsers let a driver see them.

redirectChain.description: Every address the main document was requested from on the way to finalUrl, first request first, finalUrl last. Browsers stop following redirects at about 20, so the list is short. Lets the engine check each hop against an operator's address rules. Absent when the driver cannot see the hops (classic WebDriver shows only the final address).

remoteAddress.description: The IP address the browser connected to for this request, when the browser reports it. Absent when unknown.

script.description: A JavaScript expression that evaluates to a function. The driver calls it with arg and returns its JSON-serialisable result.

arg.description: Any JSON value, passed to the function.

allFrames.description: Run in every frame the driver can reach. Default false.

awaitPromise.description: The function may return a Promise: wait for it and give its resolved value. A rejected Promise is an eval_failed error for that frame. Only drivers whose capabilities say evalAsync accept it; others refuse it with eval_failed. timeoutMs bounds the wait. Default false.

FrameInfo.description: One frame of the page. box is where the frame element sits in the top-level page and is absent for the main frame.

id.description: 'main' for the top frame. Otherwise unique within the session.

crossOrigin.description: True when the frame's origin differs from the top page's.

FrameEvalResult.description: Exactly one of value or error is present.

error.description: Why the script could not run in this frame.

results.description: One entry per frame, main frame first.

RequestsFailed.description: Only from a driver whose capabilities say failedRequests. Requests for scripts, styles, fetch/XHR data and frames that failed (a network error, or an HTTP status of 400 or more) since the last page.goto began. Cumulative, so the latest answer covers the whole load. Pictures, fonts and media are not counted, and neither are requests cancelled by a navigation.

urls.description: The first five failed addresses, with the query and fragment removed by the driver.

ScrollWait.description: What to wait for after scrolling. animations: the page height is stable and animations that end have ended. height: only that the page height is stable, which is quicker and enough when no picture is taken.

PageScrollParams.description: Give exactly one of to or byY.

byY.description: Pixels to scroll down. Negative scrolls up.

height.description: Full scrollable height after the scroll.

PageScreenshotParams.description: clip is a rectangle in top-level page coordinates and requires the clipScreenshot capability.

path.description: Absolute path of the PNG file the driver must write.

fullPage.description: Default false: only the current viewport.

PageActParams.description: Performs one action on one element and reports what it did. Component extraction never sends it. A driver whose capabilities list no actionKinds answers it with `unsupported`; a session opened without a policy answers `invalid_params`.

value.description: Text to type, option to select, or key to press.

timeoutMs.description: How long to wait for the element and for the action itself. Default 10000.

ActNavigation.description: The main document was loaded because of the action.

status.description: HTTP status of the main document, when the driver can see it.

ActDownload.description: A download the action started. The driver cancels it: the file is never stored.

text.description: Cut to 500 characters, with query and fragment removed from any address in it.

source.description: `uncaught` for an uncaught exception, `console` for console.error.

failure.description: The browser's reason when there was no response, or `blocked_by_policy` when the session's policy aborted the request.

quiet.description: False when the wait ended at its limit with the page still changing.

PageActResult.description: What an action did. Every field except `ok` is optional. A list is empty when nothing of that kind happened, or when the driver cannot observe that kind: the session's Capabilities.eventKinds says which kinds it observes, and a caller must not read an empty list as 'nothing happened' for a kind the session does not list. Readers in some languages cannot tell an absent list from an empty one, so no reader may depend on the difference.

url.description: The address of the page after the action and after settling.

popups.description: Addresses of new pages the action opened. The driver closes them. A page the policy stopped is given as the address it was going to, not that of the error page the browser shows instead, and a page with no address (one that became a download) as `about:blank`.

domChanged.description: The page changed because of the action: it navigated, or a mutation observer saw, in some frame, more changes of some kind than three times what the page changes of that kind by itself at rest, over the time the action took. The kinds are elements added or removed, text, attributes other than `style`, and `style` changes that show or hide something (`display` or `visibility`). A style change that only moves or fades an element is not counted, because pages restyle themselves that way in answer to any mouse move or scroll. A page at rest makes no changes, so for it any change counts. A change that is no bigger than the page's own noise of the same kind (a label changing on a page with a ticking clock) is not seen.

notObserved.description: The event kinds this driver could not observe for this action.

RpcErrorData.description: The data field of a JSON-RPC error from a driver or the engine.

kind.description: Known values: timeout, navigation_failed, unsupported, session_not_found, eval_failed, version_mismatch, invalid_params, invalid_request, blocked_url, busy, internal, element_not_found.
